Not quite. The evidence supports a narrower statement: no tree-cover loss event of 0.5 ha or more was detected within ASSET-C (374.8 ha) between 2021 and 2025. Valid data covered 100% of the asset.

It does not show that nothing changed at all. Small losses under 0.5 ha, losses at edges, or changes narrower than the 30 m pixels could be missed. The check also covers only 2021–2025 against a 2020-12-31 baseline, so it says nothing about other periods. Nor does it amount to a compliance finding, such as "deforestation-free."

For context, about 43.3 ha (11.55% of the asset) was forest in 2020, per JRC data.

A fair summary: "No significant (≥0.5 ha) tree-cover loss detected since 2020," not "unchanged."
